assumptions: Assay compatibility controls (capture-reagent buffer compatibility and spike-in recovery) are used to exclude reagent interference as a source of signal loss.
Simulated nasal-mucus composition and device-pass conditions reasonably approximate clinical-use stresses for initial discrimination; in vivo bridging will be required later.
This proposal treats literature as external support only and does not assert validated in vivo efficacy or exposure in large species.
biological_rationale: Rodent intranasal functional signals exist but cross-species delivery is uncertain and nasal mucus/device exposure can mask or destroy EV surface epitopes; selecting a capture-enriched fraction that resists mucin-mediated masking and testing its protected bioactivity after simulated nasal exposure provides a direct discrimination between EV-associated, membrane-protected activity and soluble secretome artifacts (inference).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Qualitative pass/fail: preserved mucin-resistant capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization + detergent/protease-sensitive activity after simulated nasal-mucus and device passage (non-numeric).
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Mucin-resistant capture-enriched intact-EV fraction (membrane-protected, activity-preserving)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A fraction that (A) shows capture-positive co-localization with particle-peak fractions using a capture chemistry selected for mucin-resistant surface display, (B) loses captured signal and activity after detergent + protease/RNase (membrane protection), and (C) preserves membrane-protected neuroinflammation-modulating activity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage, would discriminate EV-associated activity from secretome artifacts for intranasal use.
candidate_quality_attributes.uncertainty: High: novel capture approach and simulated-use stressor relevance to real-world intranasal delivery is unproven; assay interference must be controlled.

edges.competing_explanation: Protected capture-positive signal after simulated exposure could reflect selection of a minor soluble complex that co-binds capture reagents and resists mucin, not a bona fide membrane-protected EV population.
edges.missing_experiment: Direct fraction-level activity + membrane-protection readouts after simulated nasal-mucus and device passage with spike-in recovery controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV2023 recommends orthogonal intact-EV analytics and rodent studies show functional effects, but neither demonstrates survival of EV-associated signals through nasal-mucus/device stresses.

edges.competing_explanation: Loss of detectability in larger species could be driven mainly by administration or species-specific clearance rather than mucus-mediated masking or device-shear effects.
edges.missing_experiment: Short-interval in vivo recoverability after selecting fractions that pass the simulated-mucus/device preservation gate.
edges.uncertainty: High: macaque data show intranasal detectability limitations, supporting testing of mucus/device resilience, but species/formulation differences remain competing explanations.

nodes.statement: If an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localized with particle-peak fractions and detergent/protease-sensitive) is preserved in material that withstands simulated nasal-mucus and device passage, then that material more plausibly carries EV-associated, membrane-protected cargo capable of surviving the intranasal exposure milieu.

If activity in an in vitro neuroinflammation assay is present in capture-positive, membrane-protected fractions after simulated nasal-mucus/device exposure and is abolished by detergent+protease/RNase, then the activity is likely EV-associated rather than driven by soluble secretome co-isolates.

If secretome-retaining concentrates lose capture co-localization or retain detergent-insensitive activity after the same simulated exposures, then secretome-derived non-EV components explain functional signals and the material should not be advanced as an EV-enriched drug-substance for intranasal use.

competing_explanations: Apparent preservation of capture-positive signal after simulated exposure could derive from selection of a non-EV particle (lipoprotein or aggregate) that resists mucin and binds the chosen capture reagent.
Loss of signal in secretome controls after simulated exposure could reflect assay interference unique to those matrices rather than true loss of protected EVs.
dependencies: Assay-compatibility and spike-in control validation prior to interpretation
Selection and validation of a mucin-resistant capture reagent that does not itself introduce non-EV binding artifacts
Sufficient conditioned-medium production to support matrixed testing and biological replicates
design_question: Daily question: Does a mucin-resistant capture-enriched, membrane-protected small-EV fraction retain a detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage, whereas matched secretome-retaining fractions do not?
expected_measurable_effect: Qualitative preservation of capture-positive particle-peak co-localization and membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory activity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage in the mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction, and loss or detergent-insensitive activity in matched secretome-retaining controls.

experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow: (1) add spike-in tracer to each sample, (2) subject aliquots to simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage or baseline handling, (3) fractionate and identify particle-peak fractions by particle counting per fraction, (4) perform immuno-capture on intact fractions using mucin-resistant capture reagent and canonical capture reagents in parallel; quantify spike-in tracer and endogenous capture signal separately, (5) apply detergent + protease/RNase to captured material to test membrane protection (loss of signal indicates membrane protection), (6) apply capture-eluted fraction eluates to the in vitro neuroinflammation assay and measure cytokine readouts, (7) measure total protein and compute protein:particle ratio per fraction, (8) interpret co-localization and activity preservation qualitatively.
experiment.comparator: Matched paired comparisons per conditioned-medium lot (same spike-in): (1) mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction after simulated nasal-mucus incubation + device passage; (2) mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction baseline (no simulated exposure); (3) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) after simulated exposure; (4) concentrated conditioned medium baseline. Include detergent+protease-treated aliquots of capture eluates and spike-in controls for each arm.
experiment.control: Positive controls: characterized small EV preparation spiked and processed in parallel; in vitro assay positive control (dexamethasone). Negative controls: buffer-only, detergent-disrupted samples. Capture-compatibility controls: capture reagents incubated with mucin-mimic and device rinse solutions to detect assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of consistent conditioned-medium lots (same passage/bank) and sufficient material for >=3 replicates
Access to validated spike-in tracer and mucin-mimic reagents
Validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Laboratory capability to run density-fractionation/SEC, protection assays, and the in vitro neuroinflammation assay
Device-shear simulation rig or representative nasal delivery device
experiment.failure_criterion: Either (1) spike-in recovery confirms assay performance but the mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction does not reproducibly preserve capture co-localization and membrane-protected activity after simulated exposure across replicates, or (2) secretome-retaining controls show equivalent membrane-protected activity and co-localization, indicating inability to discriminate EV-associated activity.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If the experiment fails (per failure_criterion), the mucin-resistant capture enrichment does not discriminate EV-associated membrane-protected bioactivity from secretome artifacts in the simulated intranasal-exposure context; the program should treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome with respect to resilience to nasal-mucus/device stresses and deprioritize mucin-resistant capture as an identity gate.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A mucin-resistant capture-enriched intact-EV fraction will (A) co-localize capture-positive signal with particle-count peaks, (B) show loss of captured signal and activity after detergent + protease/RNase (membrane protection), and (C) preserve membrane-protected in vitro neuroinflammation-modulating activity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and representative device passage, whereas secretome-retaining controls will not.
experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative preservation (yes/no) of: (A) co-localization of particle-count peaks with mucin-resistant capture-positive fractions after simulated exposure, (B) presence of membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory effect in captured eluates that is abolished after detergent + protease/RNase, and (C) spike-in tracer recovery demonstrating assay function.
experiment.question: Does a mucin-resistant capture-enriched, membrane-protected small-EV fraction retain detergent/protease-sensitive neuroinflammation-modulating activity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage, while matched secretome-retaining fractions do not, when assay recovery is controlled with an exogenous intact-EV spike-in?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction (capture-based enrichment applied after a minimal concentration step) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from the same lot
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add to each sample prior to simulated-exposure and fractionation
Mucin-mimic matrix reagents to simulate nasal mucus (validated composition panel representative of human nasal mucus)
Representative intranasal device or device-shearing rig to simulate clinical passage

Immuno-capture reagents: mucin-resistant capture chemistry (operator-selected lectin/affinity reagent validated for low-mucin interference) plus canonical EV capture reagents (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5) for parallel comparison
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) or SEC fractionation setup and fraction collectors
Standardized in vitro neuroinflammation assay platform (e.g., LPS-stimulated human iPSC-derived microglia or primary microglia with IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex readout)
Total protein assay reagents and buffers
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio per fraction pre/post simulated exposure
Comparison of mucin-resistant capture vs canonical tetraspanin capture co-localization behavior
Spike-in recovery percentage per fraction (qualitative recovered & membrane-protected vs not recovered)
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n >= 3 conditioned-medium lots)
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across >=3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage (A) shows particle-count peak(s) that co-localize with mucin-resistant capture-positive signal, (B) yields a membrane-protected in vitro anti-inflammatory effect in the captured eluate that is abolished by detergent + protease/RNase, and (C) recovers the exogenous spike-in tracer in the same fractions indicating assay function; matched secretome-retaining controls processed identically either lack co-localizing capture-positive fractions or show detergent-insensitive activity. If these criteria are not met reproducibly, the hypothesis is falsified.

explicit_inferences: Inference: nasal-mucus and device passage are plausible, testable stressors that can mask or damage EV surface phenotype and thereby confound intracompartmental exposure and activity claims.
Inference: a capture chemistry chosen for mucin-resistant binding (operationalized below) can enrich for a subpopulation that better preserves membrane-protected cargo through simulated-use stresses.
falsification_criteria: Failure to reproducibly observe (across >=3 independent conditioned-medium preparations) preserved capture-positive particle-peak co-localization and detergent/protease-sensitive in vitro anti-inflammatory activity in the mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage, while matched spike-in controls confirm assay recovery (qualitative fail).
If secretome-retaining controls show identical membrane-protected activity and co-localization (i.e., no discrimination), hypothesis is falsified.
human_decisions_required: Select specific mucin-resistant capture chemistry (lectin vs engineered affinity reagent) and approve procurement
Approve simulated nasal-mucus composition and device-shear parameters used in testing
Decide whether a passing mucin-resistant capture-enriched fraction will be advanced into pilot-scale fractionation/yield assessment
manufacturability_assessment: The mucin-resistant capture step is proposed as an analytical/enrichment gate (research-scale) to define candidate fractions for scale evaluation; manufacturability (scalable capture chemistry, yields) must be assessed after initial proof-of-concept and is a dependency for downstream adoption.
manufacturing_rationale: Adopting a capture-enriched fraction selected for mucin-resistant surface display plus a downstream acceptance gate based on preserved membrane protection after simulated-use stresses creates a practical product-identity and compatibility gate to prioritize fractions for scale-up and CMC investment (inference).
measurement_strategy: Orthogonal fraction-level analytics with spike-in recovery controls and simulated-use stressors: particle counting per fraction (NTA/TRPS), immuno-capture detection (mucin-resistant capture reagent + canonical tetraspanin panel on parallel aliquots), detergent + protease/RNase protection assays, total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction, and in vitro neuroinflammation assay (LPS-challenged microglia IL-6/TNF-α readout) applied to eluates from capture-positive fractions.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis introduces a new discriminating test not previously proposed in the SGL-001 record: specifically evaluating a mucin-resistant capture-enriched intact-EV fraction for preservation of membrane-protected bioactivity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage, with exogenous spike-in recovery controls. Prior program hypotheses examined orthogonal capture/protection, spike-in controls, fractionation, and device/formulation compatibility separately; none tested a capture-enrichment strategy explicitly chosen to resist mucin-mediated masking and then challenged with simulated nasal-mucus + device passage as the discriminating stress. This experiment therefore provides a novel, use-condition–relevant discrimination between EV-associated and non-EV secretome contributions.
principal_risks: Assay interference by simulated mucus or formulation components producing false negatives or false positives.
Capture chemistry may enrich non-EV particles that resist mucin and confound interpretation.
Yields of capture-enriched fractions may be insufficient for manufacturable drug-substance definition even if analytically distinct.
proposed_potency_relationship: If supported, the mucin-resistant intact-EV attribute will be treated as an exploratory potency-linked identity gate (mechanism-linked, qualitative) to prioritize fractions for formal potency assay development and scale-up; it is not a validated potency assay.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Define a mucin-resistant, capture-enriched intact-EV product-identity attribute: particle-peak co-localized, capture-positive material (enriched by a capture chemistry selected for mucin-resistant surface display) that (A) is membrane-protected (loss of captured signal and activity after detergent + protease/RNase) and (B) preserves a membrane-protected in vitro neuroinflammation-modulating activity after simulated nasal-mucus incubation and device passage; use this attribute to discriminate EV-enriched drug-substance candidates from secretome-retaining concentrates for intranasal deployment.
title: Hypothesis: A mucin-resistant, capture-enriched intact-EV fraction preserves membrane-protected bioactivity after simulated intranasal exposure and discriminates EV-associated activity from secretome artifacts
